title: To amend the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to provide further transparency and accountability for the use of content that is generated by artificial intelligence (generative AI) in political advertisements by requiring such advertisements to include a statement within the contents of the advertisements if generative AI was used to generate any image or video footage in the advertisements, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The policy amends the Federal Election Campaign Act to require any political advertisement that contains AI-generated images or video footage to disclose that generative AI was used. This aims to increase transparency and accountability for AI-generated political content.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act is designed to safeguard electoral integrity by regulating the use of artificial intelligence in political messaging and advertising. It establishes guidelines, oversight, and enforcement tools to prevent AI-generated content from misleading or manipulating voters during election periods.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act mandates that any artificial intelligence system capable of modifying its own code or behavior must be continuously monitored for safety and compliance. It establishes oversight mechanisms and reporting requirements so that regulators can track how these self‑improving AIs learn and evolve over time.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act aims to curb the risk of autonomous systems behaving unpredictably or dangerously. It proposes strict regulations and oversight to make sure AI technologies are safe, transparent, and accountable.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary halt on the construction and operation of new AI‑dedicated data centers to address concerns over energy use, carbon emissions, and security risks. It aims to give lawmakers time to study the broader impacts of AI infrastructure before deciding on permanent regulations.

title: Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026 creates a federal board tasked with examining how artificial intelligence impacts cybersecurity, ensuring that AI-driven threats are identified, analyzed, and mitigated. It also establishes clear guidelines and reporting requirements to improve transparency, accountability, and cooperation between government agencies and private companies in protecting critical digital infrastructure.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 seeks to coordinate the design, use, and regulation of AI‑powered physical systems—such as robots, autonomous vehicles, and industrial machinery—to enhance safety and public confidence. It requires manufacturers, operators, and regulators to share safety data, adopt common standards, and report incidents to a federal oversight body responsible for ensuring these technologies are developed and operated responsibly.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The Make AI Work for Americans Act aims to ensure that advances in artificial intelligence benefit all American citizens by promoting ethical use, transparency, and equitable access. It proposes regulations and incentives for responsible AI development and deployment across industries to protect jobs, privacy, and public trust.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act requires government agencies to compile and publish an annual report on the development and capabilities of AI technologies within China. The report will guide policy decisions to align AI growth with national security, economic goals, and ethical considerations.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 is a law that limits the use of artificial intelligence in healthcare, ensuring that only licensed human doctors can diagnose, prescribe, and treat patients. It requires that any AI systems used in medicine receive thorough regulatory approval and that hospitals must maintain clear documentation and accountability for AI decisions.

title: To establish the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: This bill proposes creating a new Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats in the Executive Office of the President. The office would focus on identifying, assessing, and managing risks from AI and other emerging technologies.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 is a proposed law that sets clear standards to make AI systems trustworthy, transparent, and safe for society. It requires researchers and organizations to rigorously test, verify, and report AI behavior, and establishes oversight and penalties for those who fail to meet these reliability guidelines.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 sets rules for safely designing, using, and monitoring AI systems. It mandates that companies evaluate potential hazards, disclose how they manage them, and implement security safeguards to protect users and national interests.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act establishes a federal task force to improve the security and resilience of artificial intelligence systems across the United States. It aims to coordinate efforts among agencies, private companies, and stakeholders to protect AI technologies from threats and ensure they are used safely and responsibly.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: This resolution creates a Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence to oversee national AI policy and governance. The committee will guide strategy, address ethical and security concerns, and recommend regulations for the AI sector.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Hearings held.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 establishes a framework to identify, assess, and mitigate risks from AI systems. It requires developers, users, and regulators to conduct risk evaluations, report their findings, and implement safeguards that protect public safety, privacy, and economic stability.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 aims to establish comprehensive rules for the development and deployment of artificial intelligence, ensuring that AI systems are safe, transparent, and aligned with societal values. It focuses on setting standards for accountability, data usage, and human oversight to mitigate risks associated with advanced AI technologies.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 establishes regulations to assess and mitigate the environmental effects of AI systems. It requires companies to report environmental impact assessments and implement measures to reduce energy consumption and waste.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 mandates that schools incorporate AI education into their curriculum so students learn about the fundamentals, benefits, and risks of artificial intelligence. It also provides guidance and resources for teachers to develop AI literacy, aiming to prepare both educators and learners to use AI tools responsibly and ethically.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025 is a proposed law that aims to make AI development safer and more dependable by establishing guidelines for research and testing of AI systems. It seeks to promote transparency, accountability, and rigorous safety standards so that AI technologies are built to be trustworthy and aligned with societal values.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to create a pilot program that uses AI to defend critical infrastructure from cyber threats. It aims to test, evaluate, and guide the deployment of AI-based cyber defense technologies to strengthen national security.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: This act aims to integrate AI literacy into K–12 education, ensuring students understand how AI works and its societal impacts. It also sets standards for schools to prepare both teachers and students for the responsible use of AI tools.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act sets rules for using artificial intelligence to process veterans’ claims, making sure the technology is fair, accurate, and transparent. It requires oversight and safeguards so that veterans can trust that AI decisions are correct and can be reviewed by humans when needed.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 requires the Department of Veterans Affairs to disclose any AI tools used in patient care, administrative decisions, and other services, making the algorithms and decision‑making processes auditable and publicly available. The law also mandates regular reporting to Congress on AI performance, bias mitigation, and overall impact on veterans to ensure accountability and public oversight.

title: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act aims to increase public understanding of AI technologies and their impacts. It establishes programs and resources for education and outreach to inform citizens about the responsible use and potential risks of AI.

title: A resolution expressing the sense of the Senate regarding the importance of religious freedom, authoritative texts, and transparency in artificial intelligence systems.
action: Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S4958; text: CR S4951)
summary: The Senate has passed a resolution that emphasizes the need to protect religious freedom and uphold authoritative texts while engaging with artificial intelligence. It also calls for greater transparency in AI systems to ensure they align with these principles.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act aims to prevent AI systems from misleading users by requiring clear disclosures about AI involvement in content, interactions, or decisions. It establishes penalties for deceptive practices and encourages transparency and accountability for AI developers and service providers.

title: To direct the Director of National Intelligence to submit to Congress a report on the use of artificial intelligence systems to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978.
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The policy requires the Director of National Intelligence to submit a report to Congress detailing how artificial intelligence systems are used to collect, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act. This ensures congressional oversight and accountability for AI tools employed in U.S. intelligence operations.

title: Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committees on Science, Space, and Technology, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026 aims to modernize education by incorporating AI concepts into school curricula and higher‑education programs. It also seeks to equip the workforce with the skills and training needed to thrive in an AI‑driven economy.

title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 26 - 21.
summary: The Open‑Source AI Leadership Act aims to encourage the development and use of open‑source artificial intelligence technologies by establishing policies and incentives for collaboration and transparency. It seeks to position the United States as a global leader in AI by supporting open‑source initiatives, research, and ethical standards.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 seeks to curb the practice of AI firms inflating prices and manipulating labor costs. It establishes regulatory oversight to ensure fair pricing and wage standards for AI products and services.
